kept.title: Arbitrary File Read via Include Directive
kept.description: The `Include` directive in `src/mistune/directives/include.py` allows files to be read and rendered into the output. While it attempts a check using `commonpath`, the logic is insufficient to prevent traversal if `source_dir` can be misaligned or if environmental inputs are manipulated, allowing sensitive file exposure.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a Markdown file using the `.. include::` directive.
Use path traversal sequences (e.g., ../../../etc/passwd) as the directive value.
The parser reads and renders the contents of the target file into the generated HTML.
kept.impact: An attacker can read arbitrary files from the server's filesystem, leading to sensitive data exposure or configuration leaks.

kept.title: Unsafe Output File Writing in CLI
kept.description: The command-line interface in `src/mistune/__main__.py` accepts an `--output` path and blindly writes the rendered Markdown content to it. There is no validation to prevent overwriting critical system files or sensitive user data.
steps_to_exploit: Run the mistune CLI with the `--output` argument.
Point the argument to a sensitive file, such as `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` or a configuration file.
The tool truncates and overwrites the specified file with the rendered output.
kept.impact: Arbitrary file destruction or system compromise via overwriting configuration/system files.

kept.title: Unsafe URL Protocol Usage
kept.description: The HTML renderer uses a hardcoded whitelist of protocols to sanitize URLs. However, the logic in `_is_safe_url` is permissive and does not adequately account for variations or potential bypasses in URL parsing, potentially allowing `javascript:` URIs if bypasses in `urllib.parse.unquote` logic are found.
steps_to_exploit: Inject a payload like `[click](javascript:alert(1))` into the Markdown.
The renderer fails to properly neutralize the harmful URI scheme.
The resulting HTML executes arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser when clicked.
kept.impact: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in the context of the rendered document.

kept.title: Plugin Code Execution via arbitrary module loading
kept.description: The `import_plugin` function in `src/mistune/plugins/__init__.py` uses `import_module` on user-provided strings. While intended for internal plugins, the structure allows loading any arbitrary Python module available in the environment if the input string can be influenced.
steps_to_exploit: Influence the list of plugins passed to `create_markdown` (e.g., if application settings are exposed).
Pass an arbitrary module path as a plugin name.
The application executes the code within the imported module.
kept.impact: Remote Code Execution (RCE) via arbitrary module import.

kept.title: Denial of Service via ReDoS in Inline Parsing
kept.description: The `InlineParser` uses complex regex patterns for identifying markers (e.g., links, emphasis). These patterns are prone to Catastrophic Backtracking (ReDoS) when processing deeply nested or specifically crafted, long, non-matching strings.
steps_to_exploit: Supply a specially crafted long string with many overlapping Markdown markers.
The parser's regex engine enters an exponential state expansion attempting to match.
The thread or process consuming the input becomes unresponsive.
kept.impact: Denial of Service by crashing the parser or consuming excessive CPU resources.

kept.title: Use of unsafe HTML in Admonition renderer
kept.description: The `render_admonition` function in `src/mistune/directives/admonition.py` takes class attributes and directly injects them into HTML output. While `escape_text` is used, the logic surrounding it can be bypassed if the context of the injection is mishandled.
steps_to_exploit: Use an admonition directive with a crafted `class` attribute.
If the input string is not properly sanitized, the injection might escape the attribute context.
Resulting HTML reflects the user input as a class or other attribute.
kept.impact: Potentially enables XSS by breaking out of the attribute context.

kept.title: Incomplete Sanitization of HTML tags in `striptags`
kept.description: The `striptags` utility in `src/mistune/util.py` uses a regex to strip tags, which is notoriously prone to bypasses by variations in HTML tag syntax (e.g., malformed tags, whitespace, or nested null bytes).
steps_to_exploit: Supply a crafted string with malformed tags, e.g., `<img/src='x'onerror='alert(1)'>`.
The `striptags` regex fails to fully parse the tag structure.
Malicious content passes through the sanitizer and reaches the DOM.

kept.title: Potential Circular Reference DoS in Include Directive
kept.description: Although `Include` attempts to track a stack, deep recursion can still lead to stack overflow if the environment state is manipulated or if large nested structures are provided.
steps_to_exploit: Create a file that recursively includes itself or deep trees of files.
The parser exhausts memory or stack space attempting to resolve the document structure.
The process terminates.
kept.impact: Denial of Service by crashing the parser process.

kept.title: Lack of CSRF or Origin protection in `serve-doc.py`
kept.description: The `serve-doc.py` script uses `livereload`, which is meant for development environments. It binds to the default address/port without authentication, allowing remote users to trigger the rebuild process, essentially enabling a remote Command Execution vulnerability by proxy.
steps_to_exploit: Wait for the developer to run `python serve-doc.py`.
Identify the port (typically 35729 or similar).
Interact with the Livereload service to trigger build tasks which contain OS commands.
kept.impact: Execution of OS-level commands by an attacker.

kept.title: Unsafe handling of `inline_html` with escape=false
kept.description: When `escape=false` is set during `create_markdown` creation, raw HTML input is rendered directly. If this is combined with user-supplied content, it creates an immediate XSS vector.
steps_to_exploit: Ensure the Markdown parser is configured with `escape=false`.
Pass raw HTML tags with event handlers (e.g., ``).
The parser emits the payload into the output document.

kept.title: Integer Overflow/Negative handling in TOC levels
kept.description: The `TableOfContents` directive accepts numeric values for heading levels. If negative integers or invalid types are passed that bypass validation, downstream logic might throw errors, potentially leading to application crashes.
steps_to_exploit: Use `.. toc::` with invalid negative levels (e.g., `:min-level: -100`).
The system attempts to build a hierarchy based on these integers.
This triggers an unhandled `ValueError` or unexpected behavior in the rendering loop.
kept.impact: Denial of Service via application error loop.

kept.title: Implicitly Trusted Data Protocols in safe_url
kept.description: The `GOOD_DATA_PROTOCOLS` whitelist explicitly permits `data:` URI images. If misused or if the browser treats these as something other than images (e.g., SVG/HTML payloads), it can lead to XSS.
steps_to_exploit: Embed a base64 encoded SVG image with embedded scripts as a `data:` URI.
The sanitizer accepts it because it starts with `data:image/`.
The victim browser executes the script contained within the SVG.
kept.impact: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via base64 encoded payload.

kept.title: Incomplete handling of `null` in `__main__.py` CLI
kept.description: The CLI code asserts the result is a string, but the `Markdown` instance is configurable via plugins. If a plugin modifies the return type, the `assert` statement in the CLI will trigger an `AssertionError` in production.
steps_to_exploit: Configure a custom plugin that returns a list or dict instead of a string.
Run the CLI.
The program raises an `AssertionError`.

kept.title: Use of `eval`-like behavior in `getattr` lookups
kept.description: The renderer uses `getattr(self, name)` to look up rendering methods. While restricted to the instance, this is a dangerous pattern if `self` can be manipulated to call arbitrary methods of the object or its parent classes.
steps_to_exploit: The user influences the token `type` field.
The parser calls `getattr` with that field.
The system attempts to call unauthorized methods of the `HTMLRenderer` object.
kept.impact: Unexpected object behavior or potential for Information Disclosure.

kept.title: Insecure `temp` logic in `Include` directive
kept.description: The `Include` directive uses `source_file` as an environment variable to resolve paths. If `env` state is leaked or improperly initialized across parser instances, this could lead to information leaks between documents.
steps_to_exploit: Trigger concurrent parsing where one parser shares `env` state with another.
The `__file__` variable points to a secret file.
The second parser inadvertently includes the content of that secret file.
